question: Addition to the stock of capital of a firm is known as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Investment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The addition to a firm's capital stock is known as an investment.
 
• Investment is the process of purchasing assets to generate income or appreciation in the future.
 
• It can also be referred to as capital formation. 
 
• Investment is a broader concept than capital formation, which is the accounting value of new non-financial assets added to the capital stock.
 
• Investment can include all types of capital assets, such as physical property or financial assets. 
 
• Investing is the act of allocating resources, usually capital, with the expectation of generating an income, profit, or gains. Investors typically consider that a greater period of time, like months or years, is needed to generate acceptable returns. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Accumulation
 
 
• Accumulation refers to the process of gathering or increasing resources, assets, or wealth over time. It can apply to financial savings, investments, or even physical goods.
 
• In Economics: It is often associated with the gradual build-up of capital or wealth through saving and reinvesting profits.
 
• Example: A person saving money in a bank account over several years is an example of wealth accumulation.
 
 
 
• Capital Loss
 
 
• A capital loss occurs when the value of an asset decreases, and it is sold for less than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: It is the opposite of a capital gain and often impacts a firm's or individual's financial health negatively.
 
• Example: Selling a property for ₹8 lakh when it was purchased for ₹10 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital loss.
 
 
 
• Capital Gain
 
 
• A capital gain occurs when an asset increases in value and is sold for more than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: Capital gains are often taxable and are a common source of income for investors.
 
• Example: Selling stocks for ₹5 lakh that were purchased for ₹3 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital gain.
